name: Registered pension plan (RPP) deduction
eligibilitySummary: Employee contributions to a registered pension plan.
calcSummary: Deduct eligible RPP contributions reported on slips.
notes: Reduces net income.

name: RRSP deduction
eligibilitySummary: RRSP contributor with available contribution room.
calcSummary: Deduct eligible RRSP contributions up to your RRSP deduction limit.
spousalTransfer: No (spousal RRSP still deducted by contributor)
notes: Room shown on Notice of Assessment.

name: First Home Savings Account (FHSA) deduction
eligibilitySummary: FHSA holder with eligible contributions and available participation room.
calcSummary: Deduct eligible FHSA contributions (subject to FHSA limits).
notes: FHSA deduction is separate from RRSP.

name: Deduction for elected split-pension amount
eligibilitySummary: Taxpayer who elected to split eligible pension income with a spouse/partner.
calcSummary: Deduct the elected split-pension amount.
notes: Requires a joint election in tax software or form.

name: Annual union, professional or like dues
eligibilitySummary: Union/professional dues required to keep employment/professional status.
calcSummary: Deduct eligible dues paid.
notes: Keep receipts/T4 details.

name: Child care expenses
eligibilitySummary: Eligible child care expenses incurred to enable work, business, education, or certain training.
calcSummary: Deduct eligible expenses up to CRA limits; generally claimed by the lower-income spouse.
notes: Exceptions apply for students/infirm spouse.

name: Disability supports deduction
eligibilitySummary: Disability supports to work, study, or do research.
calcSummary: Deduct eligible disability supports expenses (separate from medical expense credit).
notes: Same expense generally can't be claimed twice.

name: Moving expenses
eligibilitySummary: Move at least 40 km closer to a new work location or post-secondary education.
calcSummary: Deduct eligible moving expenses up to net income earned at the new location.
carryforward: Yes (to next year if limited by income at new location)
notes: Claim based on eligible expense categories.

name: Support payments made (spousal support)
eligibilitySummary: Spousal support paid under a court order or written agreement (rules vary).
calcSummary: Deduct eligible support payments made in the year.
notes: Highly dependent on agreement/order details.

name: Carrying charges, interest expenses and other expenses
eligibilitySummary: Eligible investment-related charges/interest incurred to earn taxable investment income.
calcSummary: Deduct eligible carrying charges and interest expenses.
carryforward: Often yes (investment interest may carry forward depending on circumstances)
notes: Interest deductibility depends on use of borrowed funds.

name: Deduction for CPP/QPP contributions on self-employment income (employer portion)
eligibilitySummary: Self-employed taxpayers paying CPP/QPP.
calcSummary: Deduct eligible portion of CPP/QPP contributions on self-employment income.
notes: Employee portion is claimed as a credit on line 31000.

name: Deduction for CPP/QPP enhanced contributions on employment income
eligibilitySummary: Employees with enhanced CPP/QPP contributions.
calcSummary: Deduct eligible enhanced contributions amount.
notes: Separate from base CPP credit.

name: Other employment expenses
eligibilitySummary: Employees required by employer to incur expenses to earn employment income (conditions apply).
calcSummary: Deduct eligible employment expenses (varies).
notes: See CRA guide T4044.

name: Canadian Armed Forces personnel and police deduction
eligibilitySummary: Eligible CAF members and police officers with qualifying service.
calcSummary: Deduct eligible amount per CRA rules and certification.
notes: Specialized eligibility.

name: Security options deduction
eligibilitySummary: Employees with qualifying employee stock option benefits.
calcSummary: Deduct eligible stock option deduction when conditions met.
notes: Complex; depends on grant/exercise details.

name: Other payments deduction (workers' compensation, social assistance, etc.)
eligibilitySummary: Certain social benefits included in income but deductible for taxable income calculation.
calcSummary: Deduct eligible amounts as per slips.
notes: Often not a choice; based on slip amounts.

name: Capital gains deduction (lifetime capital gains exemption)
eligibilitySummary: Disposition of qualified small business shares and/or qualified farm/fishing property (conditions apply).
calcSummary: Deduct eligible portion of taxable capital gains up to available LCGE limit.
notes: Very complex; requires detailed eligibility analysis.

name: Northern residents deductions
eligibilitySummary: Residents of prescribed northern/intermediate zones for eligible period.
calcSummary: Deduct residency and/or travel amounts per CRA rules.
notes: Requires zone and residency qualifications.

name: Basic personal amount
eligibilitySummary: All taxpayers; claim depends on net income.
calcSummary: If net income ≤ $177,882: claim $16,129. If ≥ $253,414: claim $14,538. Otherwise use Federal Worksheet.
notes: Amounts are for 2025 tax year.

name: Age amount
eligibilitySummary: Age 65+ in the year; phased out with income.
calcSummary: Claim age amount using Federal Worksheet; reduced as net income increases.
spousalTransfer: Yes (unused portion can be transferred to spouse via amounts transferred)
notes: Transfer is typically via line 32600/amounts transferred.

name: Spouse or common-law partner amount
eligibilitySummary: Supporting a spouse/partner with low net income.
calcSummary: Base amount reduced by spouse’s net income (worksheet calculation).
notes: Claim depends on spouse’s net income.

name: Amount for an eligible dependant (equivalent-to-spouse)
eligibilitySummary: No spouse/partner and you support an eligible dependant.
calcSummary: Base amount reduced by dependant’s net income (worksheet).
notes: Cannot also claim spouse amount.

name: Canada caregiver amount (spouse/partner or eligible dependant 18+)
eligibilitySummary: Supporting an infirm spouse/partner or eligible dependant age 18+.
calcSummary: Claim per CRA rules; reduced by dependant’s net income.
notes: Part of Canada caregiver credit group.

name: Canada caregiver amount (other infirm dependants 18+)
eligibilitySummary: Supporting other infirm dependants age 18+.
calcSummary: Claim per CRA rules; reduced by dependant’s net income.
notes: May require supporting documentation/attestation.

name: Canada caregiver amount (infirm children under 18)
eligibilitySummary: Supporting an infirm child under 18.
calcSummary: Claim per CRA rules; may interact with other child-related claims.
spousalTransfer: Yes (listed as transferable under amounts transferred)
notes: Transfer via amounts transferred from spouse/partner in some cases.

name: CPP/QPP contributions through employment
eligibilitySummary: Paid CPP/QPP contributions as an employee.
calcSummary: Claim the CPP/QPP amount from slips.
notes: Part of federal non-refundable credits.

name: CPP/QPP contributions on self-employment income and other earnings (credit portion)
eligibilitySummary: Self-employed and others paying base CPP/QPP on self-employment/other eligible earnings.
calcSummary: Claim the base CPP/QPP contributions credit (employee portion).
notes: Employer portion is deductible (line 22200).

name: Employment insurance premiums through employment
eligibilitySummary: Paid EI premiums as an employee.
calcSummary: Claim EI premiums from slips.
notes: Part of federal non-refundable credits.

name: Employment insurance premiums on self-employment and other eligible earnings
eligibilitySummary: Paid EI premiums on self-employment/other eligible earnings (special program).
calcSummary: Claim EI premiums payable on self-employment and other eligible earnings.
notes: Eligibility depends on EI special benefits participation.

name: Volunteer firefighters' amount
eligibilitySummary: Volunteer firefighter with sufficient eligible volunteer hours (typically 200+).
calcSummary: Claim fixed amount per CRA rules (as an amount subject to 15% credit).
notes: Cannot claim if claiming Search & Rescue volunteers amount instead.

name: Search and rescue volunteers' amount
eligibilitySummary: Volunteer search-and-rescue with sufficient eligible hours (typically 200+).
calcSummary: Claim fixed amount per CRA rules (as an amount subject to 15% credit).
notes: Cannot also claim Volunteer firefighters amount for same year.

name: Canada employment amount
eligibilitySummary: Employment income earned in the year.
calcSummary: Claim the lesser of employment income and $1,471 (maximum for 2025).
notes: Maximum amount is indexed.

name: Home buyers' amount
eligibilitySummary: First-time home buyer (or eligible persons with disability buying a qualifying home).
calcSummary: Claim qualifying amount per CRA rules (credit based on fixed base amount).
spousalTransfer: Yes (can be shared between eligible co-buyers; max combined)
notes: Eligibility depends on first-time buyer definition and qualifying home purchase.

name: Home accessibility expenses
eligibilitySummary: Seniors (65+) or eligible persons with disability (or supporting family) for qualifying accessibility renovations.
calcSummary: Claim 15% of eligible expenses up to program limit (per CRA rules).
spousalTransfer: Yes (expenses can be claimed by eligible individual or supporting relative)
notes: Renovations must improve accessibility/safety.

name: Adoption expenses
eligibilitySummary: Adoptive parents with eligible adoption expenses during the adoption period.
calcSummary: Claim eligible adoption expenses up to annual maximum (per CRA rules).
spousalTransfer: Yes (adoptive parents can share up to the max)
notes: Claimed in the year the adoption period ends.

name: Pension income amount
eligibilitySummary: Taxpayer with eligible pension/annuity income.
calcSummary: Claim the lesser of eligible pension income and the annual maximum (typically $2,000).
spousalTransfer: Yes (unused portion can be transferred to spouse via amounts transferred)
notes: Distinct from pension splitting.

name: Disability amount for self (DTC)
eligibilitySummary: Approved Disability Tax Credit (severe and prolonged impairment; Form T2201).
calcSummary: Claim disability amount (credit at 15% of disability base amount).
spousalTransfer: Yes (unused portion may be transferred to supporting spouse/relative)
notes: Approval required via CRA DTC process.

name: Disability amount transferred from a dependant
eligibilitySummary: Supporting a dependant with an approved DTC who cannot use all of it.
calcSummary: Claim transferable portion of dependant’s disability amount.
notes: Requires supporting relationship and conditions met.

name: Interest paid on your student loans
eligibilitySummary: Interest paid on qualifying government student loans.
calcSummary: Claim eligible interest paid.
carryforward: Yes (unused amounts can generally be claimed in one of the next 5 years)
notes: Carryforward window is typically 5 years.

name: Tuition amounts
eligibilitySummary: Student with eligible tuition fees (T2202).
calcSummary: Claim eligible tuition; unused can be carried forward indefinitely; can transfer a limited amount to spouse/parent/grandparent.
spousalTransfer: Yes (limited transfer; plus spousal transfer rules for unused amounts in year)
notes: Federal education/textbook amounts were eliminated previously; tuition remains.

name: Tuition amount transferred from a child or grandchild
eligibilitySummary: Supporting parent/grandparent (or spouse) receiving a transfer from student.
calcSummary: Claim the transferred portion (subject to transfer limits).
notes: Transfer must be designated by the student on forms.

name: Amounts transferred from your spouse or common-law partner
eligibilitySummary: Spouse/partner has unused eligible credits (e.g., age, pension, disability, tuition).
calcSummary: Claim eligible transferable amounts from spouse/partner (per CRA rules).
notes: Supports spousal transfer logic for certain credits.

name: Eligible medical expenses
eligibilitySummary: Eligible medical expenses for self/spouse/dependants.
calcSummary: Claim 15% of eligible expenses above threshold (lesser of 3% of net income or a fixed amount).
spousalTransfer: Family can pool expenses; one spouse typically claims
notes: Expenses must fall within a 12‑month period ending in the year.

name: Donations and gifts
eligibilitySummary: Donations to eligible registered charities/qualified donees.
calcSummary: Credit rate depends on donation amount (higher rate above first $200).
spousalTransfer: Yes (spouses can pool and one can claim)
carryforward: Yes (unused donations can be carried forward up to 5 years)
notes: Carryforward applies for unused donations.

name: Federal dividend tax credit
eligibilitySummary: Individuals reporting eligible or other-than-eligible Canadian dividends.
calcSummary: Dividend gross-up and dividend tax credit per CRA rules.
notes: Depends on dividend type; credit reduces tax payable.

name: Federal foreign tax credit
eligibilitySummary: Foreign-source income with foreign tax paid (non-business).
calcSummary: Credit for eligible foreign taxes paid, subject to limitation.
notes: Requires documentation; limitations apply.

name: Federal political contribution tax credit
eligibilitySummary: Contributions to registered federal political parties/candidates/associations.
calcSummary: Credit based on contribution tiers up to annual maximum.
notes: Claim using official receipts.

name: Investment tax credit
eligibilitySummary: Various eligible investment tax credit programs (very specific).
calcSummary: Calculated on relevant forms; may generate refundable portion in some cases.
carryforward: Carryforward may apply depending on program
notes: Highly specialized (not common for most individuals).

name: Labour-sponsored funds tax credit
eligibilitySummary: Purchase of approved labour-sponsored venture capital corporation shares.
calcSummary: Credit based on eligible investment up to limit (per CRA rules).
notes: Availability depends on fund eligibility.

name: Refundable medical expense supplement
eligibilitySummary: Working individuals/families with low income and high medical expenses (conditions apply).
calcSummary: Refundable amount based on working income and net income (per CRA rules).
notes: Designed to help low-income earners with medical expenses.

name: Canada workers benefit (CWB)
eligibilitySummary: Low-income workers with working income; subject to eligibility rules and phase-outs.
calcSummary: 2025 maximum basic amount: $1,633 (single) or $2,813 (family). Phased out above thresholds; see CRA for details.
spousalTransfer: Family-based (couples calculated on family net income)
notes: Can also receive advance payments (ACWB).

name: Canada training credit (CTC)
eligibilitySummary: Residents aged 26–65 who meet eligibility and paid eligible tuition/fees in the year; must have CTC limit available.
calcSummary: Refundable credit equal to 50% of eligible fees paid in 2025, up to your Canada training credit limit (CTCL).
notes: Claim through Schedule 11 and line 45350.

name: Multigenerational home renovation tax credit (MHRTC)
eligibilitySummary: Eligible renovations to create a secondary unit for a senior (65+) or an adult with disability to live with a relative.
calcSummary: Refundable credit (15% of eligible costs up to program limit) as per CRA rules.
notes: Requires qualifying renovation and eligible person.

name: Employee and partner GST/HST rebate
eligibilitySummary: Employees or partners with eligible employment/business expenses that include GST/HST (conditions apply).
calcSummary: Claim GST/HST rebate amount calculated on the relevant form.
notes: Linked to employment expenses claims.

name: Eligible educator school supply tax credit
eligibilitySummary: Eligible educators with out-of-pocket eligible school supply expenses.
calcSummary: Refundable credit based on eligible expenses (per CRA rules).
notes: Keep receipts and meet educator definition.

name: Return of fuel charge proceeds to farmers tax credit
eligibilitySummary: Eligible farming business in provinces where federal fuel charge applied (eligibility depends on rules).
calcSummary: Refundable credit calculated per CRA rules/program parameters.
notes: Complex program; rules can change; verify for 2025 claims.

name: Basic personal amount
eligibilitySummary: Ontario resident at Dec 31, 2025 (for Ontario tax).
calcSummary: Claim $12,747 as base amount on ON428 (credit at 5.05%).
notes: Base amount shown on Form ON428 for 2025.

name: Age amount
eligibilitySummary: Born in 1960 or earlier (65+ in 2025); income-tested.
calcSummary: Use Worksheet ON428; maximum base amount $6,223 (credit at 5.05%).
spousalTransfer: No (Ontario uses separate transfer rules; spousal transfer is handled through ON(S2) for certain amounts)
notes: Ontario age amount uses worksheet.

name: Spouse or common-law partner amount
eligibilitySummary: Supporting a spouse/partner with low net income.
calcSummary: Maximum base amount $10,823 reduced by spouse’s net income.
notes: Ontario amounts in ON428 for 2025.

name: Amount for an eligible dependant
eligibilitySummary: No spouse/partner and you support an eligible dependant with low net income.
calcSummary: Maximum base amount $10,823 reduced by dependant’s net income.
notes: Ontario amounts in ON428 for 2025.

name: Ontario caregiver amount
eligibilitySummary: Supporting an eligible relative dependent on you because of mental/physical impairment (conditions apply).
calcSummary: Calculated using Worksheet ON428.
notes: Ontario tax info provides details and thresholds.

name: CPP/QPP contributions (Ontario credit)
eligibilitySummary: CPP/QPP contributions reported on federal return (lines 30800 and 31000).
calcSummary: Claim amounts from federal lines 30800 and 31000 on ON428; credit at 5.05%.
notes: Ontario uses federal contribution amounts.

name: Employment insurance premiums (Ontario credit)
eligibilitySummary: EI premiums through employment and on self-employment (federal lines 31200 and 31217).
calcSummary: Claim EI premium amounts on ON428; credit at 5.05%.
notes: Ontario mirrors federal EI premium credit base.

name: Adoption expenses (Ontario amount)
eligibilitySummary: Ontario adoption expenses (eligible; Ontario-specific maximum for certain claims).
calcSummary: Claim eligible adoption expenses amount on ON428 (adds to non-refundable credit base).
notes: Ontario tax info notes max $15,551 per child in year finalized under Ontario rules.

name: Pension income amount (Ontario)
eligibilitySummary: Eligible pension income (federal line 31400).
calcSummary: Claim the lesser of federal line 31400 and $1,762.
spousalTransfer: No (Ontario relies on pension splitting rather than transfer)
notes: Max shown on ON428.

name: Disability amount for self (Ontario)
eligibilitySummary: Approved disability amount for self (federal eligibility).
calcSummary: If 18+ at end of year: claim $10,298; if under 18 use Worksheet ON428.
spousalTransfer: Yes (unused portion may transfer to spouse/parent under rules)
notes: Base amount shown on ON428.

name: Disability amount transferred from a dependant (Ontario)
eligibilitySummary: Supporting a dependant with an approved disability amount who cannot use it fully.
calcSummary: Claim transferable portion per Worksheet ON428 and CRA rules.
notes: Special rules if different province of residence.

name: Interest paid on student loans (Ontario)
eligibilitySummary: Interest on eligible student loans (federal line 31900).
calcSummary: Claim the amount from federal line 31900; credit at 5.05%.
carryforward: Yes (generally can be claimed within 5 years if unused federally)
notes: Ontario mirrors federal student loan interest base.

name: Unused tuition and education amounts (Ontario)
eligibilitySummary: Student with unused Ontario tuition amounts (Schedule ON(S11)).
calcSummary: Claim current-year and/or carryforward tuition amounts; calculated on Schedule ON(S11).
spousalTransfer: Yes (student may transfer limited amount to spouse/parent; separate schedule)
notes: Ontario tuition uses Schedule ON(S11).

name: Amounts transferred from spouse or common-law partner (Ontario)
eligibilitySummary: Spouse/partner has unused eligible provincial credits transferable to you.
calcSummary: Claim transferable amounts using Schedule ON(S2).
notes: Spousal transfer logic for Ontario credits uses ON(S2).

name: Medical expenses (Ontario)
eligibilitySummary: Eligible medical expenses for self/spouse/children and other dependants (Ontario variations apply).
calcSummary: Claim eligible medical expenses; threshold is lesser of $2,885 or 3% of net income (as per ON428).
spousalTransfer: Family can pool expenses; one spouse typically claims
notes: Ontario has specific maximums for attendant care/adapted van/moving; see ON-tax-info.

name: Donations and gifts (Ontario)
eligibilitySummary: Charitable donations claimed federally (Schedule 9).
calcSummary: Ontario credit uses 5.05% on first tier and 11.16% on second tier (per ON428).
spousalTransfer: Yes (spouses can pool and one can claim)
carryforward: Yes (donations generally carry forward 5 years federally and provincially)
notes: Ontario uses federal Schedule 9 amounts.

name: Ontario dividend tax credit
eligibilitySummary: Ontario residents reporting taxable Canadian dividends.
calcSummary: Calculated using Worksheet ON428; reduces Ontario tax otherwise payable.
notes: Distinct from federal dividend tax credit.

name: Provincial foreign tax credit (Ontario)
eligibilitySummary: Foreign-source income with foreign tax paid exceeding federal foreign tax credit limit.
calcSummary: Calculate using Form T2036.
notes: Ontario tax info describes claiming process.

name: Ontario tax reduction
eligibilitySummary: Low-income Ontario residents meeting residency and other conditions; not available in some cases (e.g., bankruptcy, not Ontario resident Dec 31).
calcSummary: Calculated in ON428 Part C; reduces Ontario tax otherwise payable.
spousalTransfer: Family-based (only higher net-income spouse can claim certain dependants reductions)
notes: Not a 'credit' but materially reduces Ontario tax payable.

name: Low-income Individuals and Families Tax (LIFT) credit
eligibilitySummary: Ontario residents with employment income meeting eligibility conditions.
calcSummary: Calculated on Schedule ON428-A and reduces Ontario tax payable.
spousalTransfer: No (each spouse with employment income can claim their own)
notes: Ontario tax information page outlines conditions.

name: Community food program donation tax credit for farmers
eligibilitySummary: Ontario resident who (or spouse) is a farmer and made qualifying donation of Ontario farm products to eligible community food program.
calcSummary: Credit = 25% of qualifying donations amount that is also claimed as charitable donation.
spousalTransfer: Yes (donations can be pooled; farmer definition applies)
notes: Requires also claiming donation on federal Schedule 9 and ON428 donations line.

name: Ontario fertility treatment tax credit
eligibilitySummary: Ontario residents with eligible medical expenses for fertility treatment.
calcSummary: Credit = 25% of eligible fertility treatment medical expenses (max $5,000 credit).
notes: Refundable even if no tax payable.

name: Ontario childcare access and relief from expenses (CARE) tax credit
eligibilitySummary: Ontario families claiming federal child care expenses deduction and meeting CARE eligibility.
calcSummary: Calculated on Schedule ON479-A; refundable (income-tested).
notes: Must complete ON479-A to calculate.

name: Ontario seniors care at home tax credit
eligibilitySummary: Ontario residents age 70+ (or spouse 70+) with eligible medical expenses for senior care; income-tested.
calcSummary: Calculated on ON479 using medical expenses from ON428 line 58769; max $1,500 credit and phased out by family net income.
spousalTransfer: Family-based (one claim for both spouses in many cases)
notes: Refundable even if no tax payable.

name: Ontario seniors' public transit tax credit
eligibilitySummary: Ontario seniors (65+) with eligible public transit expenses.
calcSummary: 15% of eligible transit costs up to $3,000 (max $450).
notes: Refundable.

name: Ontario political contribution tax credit
eligibilitySummary: Contributions to Ontario registered political parties/candidates/associations.
calcSummary: Use Worksheet ON479; max $1,666.82 credit (fully refundable).
notes: Refundable even if no tax payable.

name: Ontario focused flow-through share tax credit
eligibilitySummary: Investments in eligible Ontario mining flow-through shares with renounced exploration expenses.
calcSummary: Credit = 5% of total expenses from Form T1221.
notes: Refundable.

name: Ontario co-operative education tax credit
eligibilitySummary: Businesses/partnerships (including unincorporated) hiring eligible co-op students in Ontario.
calcSummary: 25% or 30% of eligible expenditures depending on prior-year wages; max $3,000 per student placement.
notes: Although business-focused, it can be claimed on personal return for unincorporated businesses.

name: Ontario Energy and Property Tax Credit (OEPTC)
lineForm: Form ON-BEN (2026 entitlement based on 2025 return)
eligibilitySummary: Ontario resident Dec 31, 2025 who paid eligible rent/property tax or certain other housing costs (see ON-BEN).
calcSummary: Apply using ON-BEN; entitlement is paid separately from tax refund (income-tested).
spousalTransfer: Spousal rule: only one spouse/partner can apply for both of you (with exceptions for involuntary separation).
notes: OEPTC is a component of the Ontario Trillium Benefit (OTB).

name: Northern Ontario Energy Credit (NOEC)
lineForm: Form ON-BEN (2026 entitlement based on 2025 return)
eligibilitySummary: Ontario resident in Northern Ontario Dec 31, 2025 with eligible housing/energy costs (see ON-BEN).
calcSummary: Apply using ON-BEN; entitlement is paid separately (income-tested).
spousalTransfer: Spousal rule: only one spouse/partner can apply for both (exceptions apply).
notes: NOEC is a component of OTB.

name: Ontario Sales Tax Credit (OSTC)
eligibilitySummary: Low-to-moderate income Ontario residents; no separate application required.
calcSummary: CRA determines entitlement automatically; paid separately (often monthly) as part of OTB.
spousalTransfer: For families, paid to the person whose return is assessed first.
notes: ON-BEN notes OSTC does not require application.

name: Ontario Senior Homeowners' Property Tax Grant (OSHPTG)
lineForm: Form ON-BEN (2026 OSHPTG based on 2025 return)
eligibilitySummary: Age 64+ on Dec 31, 2025 and owned/occupied an Ontario principal residence with property tax paid for 2025 (see ON-BEN).
calcSummary: Apply via ON-BEN; paid separately from tax refund; income-tested.
spousalTransfer: Spousal rule: only one spouse/partner can apply for both in many cases.
notes: CRA OSHPTG Q&A confirms application via ON-BEN for 2026 OSHPTG using 2025 return.

name: Ontario Child Benefit (OCB)
eligibilitySummary: Low-to-moderate income families with children under 18; paid with Canada Child Benefit.
calcSummary: For July 2025–June 2026: up to $143.91/month per child under 18; partial benefit above adjusted family net income $26,364.
notes: Paid together with CCB as a single monthly payment.

name: GST/HST credit
eligibilitySummary: Canadian residents with low/modest income; generally 19+ (or under 19 with spouse/child).
calcSummary: CRA automatically determines eligibility when you file; quarterly tax-free payments.
notes: Not claimed as a line item; based on return assessment.

name: Canada child benefit (CCB)
eligibilitySummary: Eligible families responsible for children under 18; must file returns; CRA administers.
calcSummary: Tax-free monthly payment; amount depends on number/ages of children and adjusted family net income.
notes: Provincial programs (like OCB) may be included with CCB payment.

name: Child disability benefit (CDB)
eligibilitySummary: Child under 18 eligible for Disability Tax Credit; family eligible for CCB.
calcSummary: For July 2025–June 2026: up to $3,411 per eligible child; reduced when adjusted family net income exceeds threshold.
notes: Paid with CCB as an add-on.

name: Canada Carbon Rebate (CCR) for individuals (stopped March 15, 2025)
eligibilitySummary: Program ended: federal fuel charge and CCR for individuals stopped March 15, 2025.
calcSummary: No further quarterly CCR payments after April 2025 payment.
notes: Included for completeness: relevant for prior-year filings only (2021–2024) per CRA.

name: Advanced Canada workers benefit (ACWB)
eligibilitySummary: Eligible recipients of Canada Workers Benefit may receive advance payments.
calcSummary: Advance payments are credited against total CWB entitlement when filing the return.
notes: Reported on return to reconcile with final CWB calculation.

name: Ontario Trillium Benefit (OTB) (bundle)
lineForm: Based on ON-BEN and return assessment
eligibilitySummary: Ontario residents eligible for one or more components (OSTC, OEPTC, NOEC).
calcSummary: Payments issued separately from tax refund; monthly or single payment option available.
spousalTransfer: Family-based; spousal application rules apply for OEPTC/NOEC
notes: ON-BEN is used for OEPTC/NOEC/OSHPTG; OSTC is automatic per ON-BEN.
